title: Species & areas I: protected areas, wetlands, law

questions.q:
With reference to protected areas under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, consider the following statements:
1. The boundaries of a National Park can be altered only on a resolution passed by the State Legislature.
2. Grazing of livestock is permitted inside a National Park but not inside a Wildlife Sanctuary.
3. A Community Reserve can be declared on private or community land.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Section 35(5) bars any change to a National Park boundary except on a State Legislature resolution, and Community Reserves (introduced in 2002) can be created on private or community land, unlike Conservation Reserves, which need Government land. Statement 2 is reversed: grazing is prohibited in a National Park, whereas a Sanctuary allows regulated grazing and entry under the Chief Wildlife Warden.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Site : Location or feature
1. Patna Bird Sanctuary : Etah district, Uttar Pradesh
2. Chhari-Dhand Wetland Reserve : Edge of the Banni grasslands, Kutch
3. Asan Wetland Conservation Reserve : Confluence of the Asan and Ganga rivers, Uttarakhand
4. Hope Island : Sand spit within Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary, Andhra Pradesh
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Asan is at the confluence of the Asan and the Yamuna, and has been a Ramsar site since 2020. Patna (founded 1991) is the smallest bird sanctuary in UP; Chhari-Dhand lies beside the Banni grasslands and the Rann of Kutch; Hope Island is a 16-km sand spit built from Godavari-delta sediment that shelters Kakinada Port from storm surges.
questions.s: SPP notes C (CA 2026: Vision IAS, Shankar IAS)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about wetland law in India:
1. Designation of a wetland as a Ramsar site by itself creates a statutory protection regime in India.
2. The Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017 retained the explicit list of prohibited activities that the 2010 Rules contained.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. Ramsar listing carries no statutory protection by itself; protection comes from domestic laws. The 2017 Rules, made under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, replaced the 2010 Rules with decentralised State Wetland Authorities and dropped the explicit prohibited list; their validity is under challenge in the Supreme Court, and the Court's mining orders now fill part of the gap.
questions.s: SPP notes C (CA Aug 2026, Shankar pp. 231-233)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about mining near protected areas and wetlands:
1. The Supreme Court has barred mining within 1 km of the boundary of National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries, with a larger Eco-Sensitive Zone prevailing where one is notified.
2. The 10-km restriction on mining around the Asan Wetland Conservation Reserve was imposed by the National Green Tribunal.
3. The Wetlands Rules, 2017 prescribe a mandatory 10-km no-mining buffer around every Ramsar site.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The Supreme Court's interim order of 14 February 2024 in the Asan matter (not the NGT) required prior permission from the NBWL Standing Committee and/or MoEFCC for mining within 10 km of the reserve, and the principle has since been extended to all wetland conservation reserves. The 2017 Rules fix no buffer at all, so the Court's order is a judicial layer.
questions.s: SPP notes C (CA Aug 2026, Shankar pp. 231-233)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs) is correct?
o: They can be declared only around National Parks and never around Wildlife Sanctuaries
They are notified by the State Governments under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and every ESZ is exactly 10 km wide
They are notified by the Central Government under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 as a transition zone, and their width is site-specific though generally up to about 10 km
All industrial and commercial activity is permanently prohibited in every ESZ
questions.e: ESZs are notified by the Centre (MoEFCC) under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and act as a shock absorber between a protected area and its surroundings; width and permitted activities are fixed in each notification. MoEFCC recently notified one around Kumbhalgarh WLS in Rajasthan. Mining within 1 km of a National Park or Sanctuary is barred by the Supreme Court, and a larger ESZ prevails where notified.
questions.s: SPP notes A, C (CA 2026: Vision IAS p. 76)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Item : Detail
1. First appearance of the term 'OECM' : Aichi Biodiversity Targets, 2010
2. Formal recognition of OECMs by the CBD : 2018
3. Agencies identifying and mapping OECMs in India : MoEFCC, National Biodiversity Authority and UNDP
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. OECMs are areas outside formal protected areas that deliver long-term biodiversity outcomes through ongoing human management, and together with protected areas they are central to India's '30 by 30' commitment under the Global Biodiversity Framework. Sites are reported to UNEP-WCMC's World Database on Protected Areas, with a two-step consent process proposed for communities.
questions.s: SPP notes A (CA Aug 2026, Shankar pp. 236-238)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Biosphere Reserves in India:
1. All 18 notified Biosphere Reserves are included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
2. The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve in Himachal Pradesh was among the recent entries to that World Network, in September 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. India has 18 notified Biosphere Reserves covering 91,425 sq km, of which 13 are in the World Network, the Cold Desert BR (HP) being a recent inclusion. A Biosphere Reserve has a core, buffer and transition zone (static) and is a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere designation, not a statutory category under the Wildlife (Protection) Act.
questions.s: SPP notes A (CA Jan 2026, Shankar pp. 7-8)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about India and the Ramsar Convention is correct?
o: The Convention was adopted at Ramsar, Iran in 1971 and India has been a Contracting Party since 1982
India has more Ramsar sites than any other country in the world
Glaw Lake in Assam became India's 101st Ramsar site
Every Ramsar site in India is a notified Wildlife Sanctuary
questions.e: Ramsar dates from 1971 and India joined in 1982. India has the most sites in Asia but ranks third globally. Glaw Lake in Arunachal Pradesh (not Assam) became the 101st and the State's first. Ramsar sites need not be sanctuaries: Sukhna in Chandigarh is a man-made reservoir. Sources give different tallies at different dates: 98 (January 2026), 99 (with Shekha Jheel), 101 (August) and 103 (October, with Sukhna and Sauj Jheel).
questions.s: SPP notes C (CA 2026, Shankar pp. 7-8, 231-233; Recitals pp. 101-102)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about recent Ramsar additions:
1. Sukhna Wetland is the first Ramsar site of the Union Territory of Chandigarh.
2. Mainpuri is the only district in India with two Ramsar sites.
3. Shekha Jheel in Aligarh is a perennial freshwater body that came into being after the Upper Ganges Canal was built in 1852.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Sukhna is a 1958 reservoir at the Shivalik foothills on the Central Asian Flyway. Sauj Jheel, a floodplain lake near Saman Bird Sanctuary, makes Mainpuri the only district with two sites. Shekha Jheel, reported by one source as the 99th site, is also a BirdLife Important Bird Area known for the Indian river tern and the sarus crane.
questions.s: SPP notes C (CA 2026, Vision IAS p. 67; Recitals pp. 101-102)

questions.q:
With reference to India's wetland and coastal programmes, consider the following statements:
1. The National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems (NPCA), launched in February 2013, merged the earlier National Lake Conservation Plan and National Wetland Conservation Programme.
2. Amrit Dharohar was announced in 2023 to promote optimal use of wetlands.
3. Mission Sahbhagita (2022) is a wetlands programme whose Save Wetlands Campaign mapped over 1.7 lakh wetlands.
4. MISHTI restored 4,536 ha of mangroves in 2025 and identified 22,560 ha of degraded mangroves in 13 States/UTs.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. NPCA is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme; Mission Sahbhagita's Save Wetlands Campaign (2023) used volunteers to map wetlands for the national wetland atlas; MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes) targets blue-carbon restoration. India also has 18 Blue Flag beaches in the 2025-26 season and the National Coastal Mission (2025-31).
questions.s: SPP notes C (CA 2026, Recitals pp. 101-102; Shankar pp. 7-8)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Blue Flag beaches in India is not correct?
o: Certification is awarded by the Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE)
Certification is awarded by UNESCO on the basis of the World Heritage criteria
India had 18 certified beaches across 7 States and 4 UTs in the 2025-26 season
It is implemented in India by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.e: The statement attributing the certificate to UNESCO is wrong. Blue Flag is an eco-label of the Denmark-based Foundation for Environmental Education, covering cleanliness, bathing-water quality, safety and sustainable management; MoEFCC implements it in India. It sits alongside MISHTI and the National Coastal Mission (2025-31) in India's coastal agenda.
questions.s: SPP notes C (CA Jan 2026, Shankar pp. 7-8)

questions.q:
Which of the following were launched or announced during Wildlife Week 2025 (2-8 October)?
1. A Centre of Excellence for Human-Wildlife Conflict Management
2. The project 'Tigers Outside Tiger Reserves'
3. The second Snow Leopard Population Assessment (SPAI 2.0)
4. Project Cheetah
questions.e: Items 1, 2 and 3 belong to Wildlife Week 2025. Project Cheetah dates from 2022 (the first African cheetahs reached Kuno that September) and was in its expansion phase by 2025. Wildlife Week also saw five species projects (including Dolphin Phase II, Sloth Bear and Gharial) and four action plans and field guides for river dolphins, tigers, snow leopards and bustards.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jan 2026, Shankar pp. 7-8)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary and Hope Island:
1. Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary lies in East Godavari district at the point where the Godavari meets the Bay of Bengal.
2. Hope Island is a 16-km sand spit formed from Krishna river sediment.
3. The island exposes Kakinada Port to storm surges by letting waves pass through.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Coringa (declared a sanctuary in 1978) is part of the Godavari mangroves. Hope Island is built from Godavari-delta sediment, not the Krishna's, and it acts as a natural breakwater that shields Kakinada, making it among the safest natural ports. Andhra Pradesh's plan for a satellite-launch facility under its Space City project raises the GS-III question of space infrastructure against mangrove ecology.
questions.s: SPP notes C (CA 2026, Vision IAS p. 76)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Kaziranga National Park:
1. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
2. The Indian soft-shell turtle, which is listed as Critically Endangered by the IUCN, was satellite-tagged there for the first time in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Kaziranga, between the Brahmaputra and the Karbi (Mikir) Hills, holds the largest population of the Indian one-horned rhinoceros; its Elevated Corridor project was inaugurated in 2026. The soft-shell turtle (Ganges softshell) was indeed satellite-tagged there, but it is IUCN Endangered, protected under Schedule I of the WPA and CITES Appendix I.
questions.s: SPP notes C, E (CA 2026, Vision IAS pp. 75, 85)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Programme or network : Figure
1. Protected Areas network, 2014 to 2025 : 745 to 1,134
2. Tiger Reserves, 2014 to 2025 : 46 to 58
3. Elephant Reserves, 2014 to 2025 : 26 to 33
4. Biosphere Reserves notified : 18, covering 91,425 sq km
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four pairs are correct. The newest tiger reserve in the series is Madhav in Madhya Pradesh (the 58th); 8,610 sq km were added to elephant reserves in the period, and 13 of the 18 Biosphere Reserves are in UNESCO's World Network. Wildlife corridors were identified to link habitats.
questions.s: SPP notes A, B (CA Jan 2026, Shankar pp. 7-8)

questions.q: Which one of the following Indian Ramsar sites is on the Montreux Record, the register of sites where an adverse change in ecological character has occurred, is occurring or is likely to occur?
questions.e: Loktak, in Manipur, is the Indian site on the Montreux Record, a list kept under the Ramsar Convention that flags sites needing priority conservation attention. Inclusion is voluntary and is meant to draw technical and financial help. Chilika was listed in 1993 and removed in 2002 (static).
